interpretation: Raw deletion classification is strongly exposed by annotated interval duration, but not by simple energy or silence measures. Speaker/phone/duration matching removes the duration advantage and retains 782 validation pairs across 33 phones and all six validation speakers. This supports one tightly controlled conditional experiment, but does not yet confirm an acoustic deletion signal.

r4_1_design.experiment: one conditional expected-phone compatibility model; not a blind audio-only deletion CNN
r4_1_design.input: uniform 0.30 s audio log-mel plus canonical expected-phone token, with no duration/start/end/speaker/relation features
r4_1_design.target: non-deletion=0 for clean correct/substitution; deletion=1 for DELETION_ELIGIBLE
r4_1_design.loss: TRAIN-only class-weighted CrossEntropy; standard shuffled loader; no sampler, focal loss, or augmentation
r4_1_design.split: unchanged S1 TRAIN/VALIDATION; R4 TEST closed
mandatory_controls: full validation and strict speaker+phone+10ms-duration-matched validation
compare against frozen TRAIN-fit duration baseline
fixed input tensor length and identical crop/padding for both classes
